title: Feature-flagged endpoint evolution & staged shutdown manifest
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, timeline and communication plan for evolving a legacy inference endpoint family (legacy-generate/*) into the unified 'generate' contract and then decommissioning the legacy endpoints. The approach uses server-side feature flags, a short compatibility shim, SDK adapters, and clear telemetry gates so we can measure migration progress and safely enforce a shutdown window.
background: Multiple older clients and third-party SDKs still call legacy-generate endpoints that predate the unified inference contract. Maintaining both code paths increases runtime complexity and testing surface. Rather than immediate removal, we will run a staged migration with opt-in compatibility and a forced migration window, minimizing customer disruption while reclaiming technical debt.
scope_in_scope: Introduce server-side feature flag to route legacy endpoint traffic to compatibility shim
Publish exact migration contract and SDK adapter code for official Redwood SDKs (JS, Python, Go)
Expose migration telemetry dashboards and automatic health gates
Run internal and customer canaries and measure per-customer migration progress
Provide console banners, API response warnings, and support playbooks
out_of_scope: Automatic client rewrites for third-party closed-source SDKs
Changes to model behavior or token-level pricing
Migration of internal tooling not calling public endpoints (handled separately)
requirements: R1: New unified 'generate' route must accept legacy payloads via adapter without semantic regressions
R2: Compatibility shim must add deprecation header and emit structured telemetry for each request
R3: Feature flag must allow 0%->100% ramp over region/customer cohorts with rollback capability
R4: SDKs must include an adapter that logs a single migration warning per session and a migration helper CLI
R5: Console must show per-customer migration % and an auto-generated migration checklist for customers with >10k monthly calls
acceptance_criteria: AC1: End-to-end tests validate 100% parity on a representative prompt suite across legacy and unified endpoints (baseline regression <0.5% diff on normalized outputs)
AC2: Telemetry pipelines emit 'legacy_call' and 'shim_routed' events and dashboard shows per-customer drop below 5% legacy usage before forced cutoff
AC3: SDK adapters available in JS/Python/Go with migration docs and sample PRs; official SDKs release versions that remove legacy-only helpers by forced cutoff date
AC4: Internal canary (5% traffic) and open beta (25% traffic) show no production-severity errors attributable to migration for 14 days before ramp
AC5: Rollback to legacy routing via feature flag possible within 30 minutes, with documented runbook and automated alerting
rollout_milestones: Customer opt-out grace & support window open: 2026-05-05 to 2026-07-05
Compatibility shim soft-sunset (no longer recommended, warnings only): 2026-07-06
migration_steps: Step 1: Publish compatibility contract doc and sample transformations for common payload shapes
Step 2: Release official SDK adapters that convert legacy payloads client-side (minor patch releases)
Step 3: Turn on server-side shim behind feature flag for internal traffic only and validate metrics
Step 4: Expand shim to canary customers and run paired-request experiments comparing outputs
Step 5: Notify customers in scaffolded waves with migration checklists and migration assistant invites
Step 6: After open beta stability, schedule forced cutoff and remove legacy code paths in runtime with ability to enable for 30 minutes if rollback needed
client_sdk_changes: Add adapter 'legacyToUnified' helper in JS/Python/Go SDKs
Deprecation logs: console.warn or logger.warn once per process/session when adapter used
New SDK versioning policy note: adapters are supported for 90 days after forced cutoff
Provide migration CLI 'rwd-migrate-requests' that replays representative request sets against unified endpoint and produces diff reports
monitoring_and_telemetry: Track metrics: legacy_calls_total, shim_routed_total, shim_error_rate, unified_mismatch_rate (normalized output diff)
Gates: block ramp if shim_error_rate > 0.5% for 5-minute window or unified_mismatch_rate > 1% over 1,000 paired requests
Dashboards: per-region and per-customer migration percent, active adapters by SDK version, top 20 customers still using legacy endpoints
Automated alerts: paging for on-call if shim_latency_95 > +200ms relative to baseline or shim_error_rate triggers gate
communication_plan: Pre-announcement: blog + docs summary and migration timeline 60 days before beta
Console in-product banner: show migration status and link to checklist for affected projects
Targeted emails: top 50 customers by legacy traffic with assigned success engineer outreach
SDK release notes and migration guide pages with code snippets and troubleshooting
Webinar: two technical sessions for integrators during open beta
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large customers with custom proxies fail to detect deprecation headers. Mitigation: targeted outreach and telemetry-based escalations with account SLAs.
Risk: Semantic drift between legacy and unified outputs for edge prompts. Mitigation: paired-request regression harness and quick rollback flag
Risk: Third-party SDKs lag in adoption. Mitigation: provide lightweight server-side shim and offer a short-term paid migration assistance engagement
Risk: Unexpected SLO regressions during ramp. Mitigation: conservative canary sizing and automated rollback thresholds
rollback_plan: Rollback is via feature flag that re-enables legacy routing. Ongoing sessions must be drained; runtime will roll traffic back to legacy paths and the on-call must trigger rollback runbook. Post-mortem required within 48 hours and freeze on further ramp until remediation.
post_cutoff_cleanup: Remove legacy route code and tests from runtime repo
Deprecate adapter code on SDK master and schedule removal 90 days after cutoff
Close related console banners and archive migration dashboards
Publish a public post-mortem summarizing impact and lessons learned
success_metrics: >95% of legacy calls migrated to unified endpoint within 60 days of open beta
Customer-reported migration issues <= 5 for top 50 customers during migration window
No P0 incidents attributable to migration during or after forced cutoff
Reduction in runtime complexity: measured as 1.2k LOC removed from endpoint routing module
